A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DistR research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, despite substantial reorganization and some caption inconsistencies in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original DistR experiments, including benchmark scores in Table 1, component scores in Appendix E, and toy and real-data visualizations.

after.justification: V2 reports original DistR benchmark results, prototype-count analyses, downstream clustering scores, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds factorized evaluation of elementwise-squared target similarities using flattened outer products, which v1 explicitly treated as nonfactorizable. This is a limited computational refinement; the DistR objective and alternating embedding/transport optimization, including both transport solvers, remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, COIL-20, PBMC, two SNAREseq views, and two Zeisel label levels, alongside the same toy/grid demonstrations. Euclidean and hyperbolic representations already appear in v1. K-means/NMI adds an assessment of the retained joint reduction-and-clustering outputs.

E2.justification: DR→C and C→DR are retained. COOT participates in v1's joint-score and component-score comparisons across all eight datasets; v2 restricts its quality comparison to best homogeneity on six datasets in Table 2, excluding it from the main trade-off and metric plots. COOT remains in runtime comparisons.

E3.justification: V1 selects configurations using its fixed combined homogeneity/silhouette score. V2 adds downstream k-means/NMI and selects trade-offs using sums of dataset-wise min-max-normalized metrics; Table 2 instead selects best homogeneity. Appendix E.1 also changes the reported mirror-descent epsilon validation rule from {0.1, 1, 10} to two stable values drawn from 10^-3 through 10^3. Runtime experiments introduce precomputation controls.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's selected-configuration tables, v2 reports extensive analyses of performance across prototype counts and homogeneity-versus-silhouette/NMI trade-offs in Appendices E.3–E.5. Appendix E.6 adds runtime comparisons with and without spectral-clustering precomputation, substantially expanding evidence about granularity sensitivity and computational practicality.

E5.justification: Five-seed/run reporting is retained. V2 additionally displays individual runs and 20th–80th percentile regions for normalized trade-off scores in Figures 3 and 14. This expands dispersion reporting without establishing an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the combined-score tables with newly reported NMI, prototype-count, trade-off, and runtime results. For example, COOT's 2D MNIST homogeneity is 2.0 (1.0) at the combined-score-selected configuration in v1 Table 4, versus 9.8 (3.0) under best-homogeneity selection in v2 Table 2. These different selection conditions do not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The main theorems and proofs in Appendices A–C retain their substance. Appendix D.1 revises the reduced-objective matrix expression, generalizes Gram factorizations to paired factors, and adds reasoning that replaces the quadratic-loss complexity term n² with min(n², ns²).

C1.justification: V2 narrows the abstract/introduction's empirical framing from explicit claims of outperforming existing approaches to demonstrating useful prototypes at different scales. The central contributions—unifying dimensionality reduction and clustering through GW and optimizing them jointly—remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly treats hyperbolic experiments as proofs of concept with optimization and hyperparameter limitations. Appendix E.7 explains why low homogeneity weakens silhouette interpretation and suggests curvature tuning. Section 4.2 also adds a rank-dependent exception to the stated limits of applying the barycenter clustering theorem directly to DistR.

D1.justification: New disclosures include V100 GPU/Xeon hardware and precomputation accounting in E.6, plus hyperbolic k-means optimization and explicit curvature/loss choices in E.7. Low-rank computation details are refined in D.1. Most libraries, initialization, preprocessing, dataset access information, and the code-with-submission statement were already provided in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds metacell and single-cell application references, including Baran, Rao, and Saelens, together with weighted-clustering and evaluation references such as Chan, Huang, and Kvålseth. Some broader survey/application citations are removed. Positioning relative to earlier GW research and COOT remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. Computation and related work are incorporated into Section 4.1, implementation material moves into the appendix, and experimental material is reorganized into E.1–E.7 with an appendix outline. These are extensive narrative and structural changes beyond added results alone.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, Figure 1's examples become side-by-side, and the embedding illustration moves from Figure 3 to Figure 5. Performance tables give way to numerous multipanel trade-off, score, and runtime plots. Some new captions are inconsistent, including Figures 10–11 describing NMI plots as silhouette plots.

improvement.justification: V1 reports quality mainly at selected configurations and provides no timing study. V2 exposes behavior across prototype counts, adds downstream NMI and runtime comparisons with precomputation controls, and qualifies hyperbolic limitations. This substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny of DistR's central summarization claims. Narrower COOT quality comparisons and caption inconsistencies are drawbacks, but do not outweigh these gains.
